units.source_text: 我被介紹給所謂的「同志」，還讓我買了一本學習手冊，聽坐在首席那位長相醜陋的青年講授馬克思經濟學。

en.t: I was introduced to so-called comrades, made to buy a study pamphlet, and listened to an ugly young man seated at the head of the room lecture on Marxist economics.

units.source_text: 可是，對我來說，那些都是再明白不過的內容了。

en.t: But to me, all of it was already perfectly obvious.

units.source_text: 他講的雖然沒錯，但人類的內心存在著更為可怕莫名的東西。

en.t: What he said was not wrong, but inside human beings there exists something still more frightening and unfathomable.

units.source_text: 說是慾望，不足以概括；說是虛榮，又不夠確切；即使把「色」與「欲」二者並列一起描述，仍不足以形容。

en.t: To call it desire is not enough; to call it vanity is not quite right; even setting lust and greed side by side still fails to describe it.

units.source_text: 我自己也弄不明白，在人世間的根基裡，總覺得不單單隻有經濟，還存在著荒唐怪談之類的事。

en.t: I do not understand it myself, but I cannot help feeling that at the root of human society there is not only economics, but also something like an absurd ghost story.
